name: David Livingstone
title: David Livingstone: calling, journeys, and a story that calls for listening
description: David Livingstone’s missionary training and his African journeys, read with attention to the communities that already lived in those places.

sections.heading: From factory work to mission
paragraphs: David Livingstone was born in Blantyre, Scotland, in 1813. As a child he worked in a cotton mill and attended classes at night. Later he studied medicine and theology. The missionary society that accepted him changed his original destination from China to southern Africa.

He arrived in South Africa in 1841 and married Mary Moffat in 1845. His path brought together missionary work, travel, and geographic observation. The timeline from his birthplace museum lets us follow these changes in activity without reducing his whole life to a single expedition.

sections.heading: The places had names and histories
paragraphs: In 1855 Livingstone saw the falls known as Mosi-oa-Tunya and gave them the name Victoria. The distinction matters: his arrival brought the place into the knowledge of certain European audiences, but African communities already knew that land and had their own relationships with it.

Livingstone denounced slavery and took part in British projects of trade and exploration. Andrew C. Ross’s summary also recalls his criticism of British policy and his dependence on African companions. He died at Chitambo in 1873. Susi, Chuma, and other companions made it possible to carry his body to the coast. These people deserve a place in the memory of his journeys.

reflection: In Philippians 2:3–4, Paul calls us to consider others and look to their interests. Applied to the meeting of cultures, that principle invites us to ask how people are named, who tells the story, and whose voices are left out when we admire a main character.

Gratitude for a calling can go hand in hand with examining its limits. To serve in another setting, we need to learn from those who live there and recognize their ability to make their own decisions. Proclaiming Christ requires caring for our relationship with our neighbor and examining the ambitions that may get mixed into our mission.
review_note: The name Mosi-oa-Tunya is kept, and we avoid speaking of the discovery of a land that was not unknown to its inhabitants. The dialogue attributed to Stanley is not repeated as fact.
